nodes.title: Divisibility submodule
nodes.statement: E_f(C)^i is the R-submodule of C^i consisting of x for which there exists y in C^(i+1) with f y=d x. No torsion-freeness is needed to define this submodule.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; f is an element of R.
C is a cochain complex of R-modules indexed by all integers; d raises degree by one.
proofSteps: Use the preimage under d of the image of scalar multiplication by f.
For sums add the witnesses; for scalar multiples multiply the witness by that scalar. Commutativity of R supplies scalar linearity.
acceptance: The ambient carrier is the existing module C^i, not a replacement module type.
The zero-divisor case is admitted for this definition only.

sources.match: This is the untwisted local submodule in Definition 6.2. The source does not require a generator in the global construction.

uses.how: A witness supplies division of the differential by f.
These submodules are the normalized terms.

nodes.title: Divided differential
nodes.statement: For x in E_f(C)^i, define δ_i(x) to be the unique y satisfying f y=d_i x, regarded as an element of E_f(C)^(i+1). This is an R-linear map.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; f is an element of R.
C is a cochain complex of R-modules indexed by all integers; d raises degree by one.
Multiplication by f is injective on every term of C.
proofSteps: Existence is the defining divisibility condition; uniqueness uses injectivity on C^(i+1).
Apply d to f y=d x. Injectivity on C^(i+2) gives d y=0, so y belongs to the next divisibility submodule.
Uniqueness applied to sums and scalar multiples proves linearity.
acceptance: Do not select arbitrary preimages without proving uniqueness.
The derivative of the selected preimage vanishes before it is re-bundled.

sources.match: An explicit affine implementation of the factored differential; division is by injective scalar multiplication, not by a field inverse.

uses.how: It is the adjacent differential of the normalized cochain complex.

nodes.title: Divisibility equation
nodes.statement: For every i and x in E_f(C)^i, f δ_i(x)=d_i x in C^(i+1).
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; f is an element of R.
C is a cochain complex of R-modules indexed by all integers; d raises degree by one.
Multiplication by f is injective on every term of C.
proofSteps: Unpack the unique preimage used to define δ_i.
acceptance: Use the equation after applying any R-linear map.

sources.match: The commutative differential square in the chosen generator.

nodes.title: Square-zero divided differential
nodes.statement: δ_(i+1) composed with δ_i is zero for every integer i.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; f is an element of R.
C is a cochain complex of R-modules indexed by all integers; d raises degree by one.
Multiplication by f is injective on every term of C.
proofSteps: The equation f δ_i(x)=d x and d²=0 give d δ_i(x)=0 by f-injectivity.
Apply the divisibility equation once more: f δ_(i+1)δ_i(x)=0. Injectivity implies the value is zero.
acceptance: Retain injectivity on both required target terms.

sources.match: Expanded verification that the displayed differential defines a complex.

nodes.title: Principal décalage complex
nodes.statement: Define the normalized principal complex E_f(C) with terms E_f(C)^i and differential δ_i. For a nonzerodivisor f in R it identifies with η_f C inside C[1/f] by x↦f^i x in degree i, using inverse powers for i<0.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; f is an element of R.
C is a cochain complex of R-modules indexed by all integers; d raises degree by one.
Multiplication by f is injective on every term of C.
proofSteps: Apply CochainComplex.of to the existing module objects and adjacent maps.
A submodule of an f-torsion-free module is f-torsion-free.
For the localized comparison, injectivity of C^i→C^i[1/f] follows from termwise f-injectivity. The map x↦f^i x has the required image and intertwines δ with d.
acceptance: The construction is indexed by Z, including negative degrees.
The normalized model alone is not the generator-independent global ideal construction.

nodes.title: Restriction of chain maps
nodes.statement: For an R-linear chain map u:C→D between termwise f-torsion-free complexes, define E_f(u):E_f(C)→E_f(D) by restricting u_i in every degree.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; f is an element of R.
C is a cochain complex of R-modules indexed by all integers; d raises degree by one.
Multiplication by f is injective on every term of C.
D is also termwise f-torsion-free; u is a chain map.
proofSteps: If f y=d x, then f u(y)=d u(x), so restriction lands in the target submodule.
The chain-map square for divided differentials follows after multiplying both sides by f and using injectivity in the target.
Bundle the components with CochainComplex.ofHom.
acceptance: This construction is on the category of complexes, prior to localization.

sources.match: The source uses the functor on chain maps; the restriction and its square are made explicit here.

nodes.statement: The image in D^i of E_f(u)_i(x) equals u_i applied to the image of x in C^i.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; f is an element of R.
C is a cochain complex of R-modules indexed by all integers; d raises degree by one.

u:C→D is an R-linear chain map and D is termwise f-torsion-free.
proofSteps: The component is the restriction of u_i; forget its membership witness.
acceptance: Use this equality to establish naturality on cycles and quotients.

nodes.title: Cycles of principal décalage
nodes.statement: Under E_f(C)^i→C^i, the cycles of E_f(C) identify with Z^i(C).
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; f is an element of R.
C is a cochain complex of R-modules indexed by all integers; d raises degree by one.
Multiplication by f is injective on every term of C.
proofSteps: If δx=0, the divisibility equation gives d x=0.
If d x=0, use the zero witness to see x belongs to E_f(C)^i; uniqueness of division gives δx=0.
acceptance: The identification is on actual submodules, before passing to cohomology.

sources.match: Local cycle calculation; tensor twists are reinstated globally.

nodes.title: Boundaries after division
nodes.statement: Within Z^i(C), the boundaries of E_f(C) are exactly the z such that f z belongs to B^i(C).
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; f is an element of R.
C is a cochain complex of R-modules indexed by all integers; d raises degree by one.
Multiplication by f is injective on every term of C.
proofSteps: If z=δy, then f z=d y is a boundary of C.
If f z=d y, then y lies in E_f(C)^(i-1) by definition, and division uniqueness gives δy=z.
acceptance: Only f-annihilated cohomology is removed; this is not removal of all f-power torsion.

sources.match: Explicit boundary criterion underlying the cohomology quotient.

nodes.title: Principal cohomology quotient
nodes.statement: There is a natural R-linear isomorphism H^i(E_f(C))≅H^i(C)/H^i(C)[f], where H^i(C)[f]=ker(f:H^i(C)→H^i(C)).
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; f is an element of R.
C is a cochain complex of R-modules indexed by all integers; d raises degree by one.
Multiplication by f is injective on every term of C.
proofSteps: Identify the cycle modules by principal-cycles.
The new boundary submodule is the inverse image of H^i(C)[f] under Z^i(C)→H^i(C), by principal-boundaries.
Apply the module quotient isomorphism theorem. Naturality follows from the component equation.
acceptance: For [Z --4→Z], f=2, H^1 becomes Z/2 rather than zero.

sources.match: The local degree twist has been trivialized by the fixed generator; the annihilator has exponent one.

nodes.title: Ideal décalage
nodes.statement: For a termwise I-torsion-free O-complex C, define η_I C in degree i as {x in C^i : d x belongs to I C^(i+1)} tensor I^⊗i, with the differential obtained by factoring d through I C^(i+1). This construction is functorial in C and independent of local generators.
hypotheses: (T,O) is a ringed topos.
I is an invertible ideal subsheaf of O, locally generated by a nonzerodivisor.
Negative tensor powers of I mean powers of its dual.
The map I tensor C^i→C^i is monic in every degree.
proofSteps: Form the divisibility subobject intrinsically as a kernel/preimage in O-modules and tensor it with the invertible sheaf I^⊗i.
Locally trivialize I=(f). The preceding normalized complex gives the differential and its square-zero identity.
If f′=u f, the comparison of normalized coordinates in degree i multiplies by u^(-i). These factors intertwine differentials and satisfy the cocycle identity.
Use the sheaf-module descent and tensor-invertible-object interface requested from E1. This is an explicit unresolved supplier, not a formalized construction.
acceptance: Keep the inherited node ID.
Negative tensor powers use the dual line, and overlap transitions must be checked.

sources.match: The global definition and source convention are retained, not replaced by a principal-only object.

uses.how: Its line twist determines the global quotient formula.
The intrinsic ideal construction specializes to (p).

Pass to the quotient, tensor with the invertible line, and use the natural cohomology formula.

nodes.statement: Construct Lη_I:D(O)→D(O) by applying η_I to termwise-flat K-flat representatives and inverting quasi-isomorphisms. On any I-torsion-free representative C, its value is represented by η_I C.
hypotheses: (T,O) is a ringed topos.
I is an invertible ideal subsheaf of O, locally generated by a nonzerodivisor.
Negative tensor powers of I mean powers of its dual.
proofSteps: Use E1 to choose strongly K-flat replacements and comparison roofs; their termwise flatness implies I-torsion-freeness.
Use quasi-isomorphism-preservation and the localization universal property to descend the complex-level construction.
Compare an arbitrary I-torsion-free representative with a strongly K-flat one and use the same invariance.

nodes.title: Lax symmetric monoidal structure
nodes.statement: Construct the natural maps Lη_I C tensor^L Lη_I D→Lη_I(C tensor^L D) and O→Lη_I O, with the associativity, symmetry and unit coherence of a lax symmetric monoidal functor.
hypotheses: (T,O) is a ringed topos.
I is an invertible ideal subsheaf of O, locally generated by a nonzerodivisor.

proofSteps: Choose strongly K-flat models C,D. Locally send x tensor y in normalized degrees i,j to x tensor y in degree i+j. The signed Leibniz identity puts it in the required divisibility submodule.
Globally combine the line factors I^⊗i tensor I^⊗j→I^⊗(i+j).
The complexes η_I C and η_I D need not be K-flat. Resolve them before forming the derived source tensor and map that tensor to the ordinary tensor used by the element-level formula.
Check coherence before passing to localization; E1 supplies independence of resolution and monoidal coherence in the shared category.

nodes.title: Bockstein complex
nodes.statement: Construct B_I(C) with degree-i term H^i(C tensor^L O/I) tensor I^⊗i and differential the connecting map for 0→I/I²→O/I²→O/I→0, with its conormal factor absorbed in the next line twist.
hypotheses: (T,O) is a ringed topos.
I is an invertible ideal subsheaf of O, locally generated by a nonzerodivisor.
Negative tensor powers of I mean powers of its dual.
C is an object of D(O).
proofSteps: Use a termwise I-torsion-free model to compute reduction by the two-term flat resolution of O/I.
On a principal chart a cocycle modulo f is lifted to x with d x=f y; send its class to the class of y modulo f. Changing the lift or a cohomology representative changes y by a boundary.
Since d y=0 by f-injectivity, repeating the boundary operation gives zero.
The line factors make this description independent of a chosen generator.
acceptance: The differential is the Bockstein, not zero by definition.
The construction does not assume that C itself has torsion-free cohomology.

sources.match: This is the actual differential complex appearing on the right of the reduction comparison.

uses.how: The Bockstein records the differential, not only graded Hodge–Tate groups.

nodes.statement: There is a natural quasi-isomorphism (Lη_I C) tensor^L O/I→B_I(C). On an I-torsion-free representative it is induced by sending a divided-differential term to its cohomology class modulo I.
hypotheses: (T,O) is a ringed topos.
I is an invertible ideal subsheaf of O, locally generated by a nonzerodivisor.
Negative tensor powers of I mean powers of its dual.
C is an object of D(O).
proofSteps: Both C/I and (η_I C)/I compute their derived reductions: the flat resolution [I→O] is bounded and scalar multiplication is termwise injective. This is not an assertion that the complexes themselves are K-flat.
The assignment x↦[x mod f] in normalized coordinates kills fE and intertwines the divided differential with β.

Injectivity on cohomology: write a reduced cycle x with d x=f² z. If [x] is a Bockstein boundary, choose y with d y=f w and x−w=d v+f a. Replacing y by y+f v gives x−δ(y+f v)=f a. Differentiation gives f d a=f² z, so a belongs to E and x is a boundary modulo fE.
Surjectivity: a β-closed class has a lift x with d x=f y and y=d z+f w. Replace x by x−f z. Its differential is f² w; d w=0, so the corrected lift is a cycle of E/fE.
The argument works in every degree with the prescribed line factors and is natural under chain maps.
acceptance: The [Z --p→Z] test is acyclic on both sides; replacing β by zero would fail it.
The chain-map and injectivity/surjectivity helper declarations need further splitting in the continuation.

sources.match: Inherited comparison with an explicit lifting proof; full declaration-level splitting of the general sheaf proof remains a gap.

nodes.title: Preservation of derived completeness
nodes.statement: If J is a locally finitely generated ideal and C is derived J-complete, then Lη_I C is derived J-complete.
hypotheses: (T,O) is a ringed topos.
I is an invertible ideal subsheaf of O, locally generated by a nonzerodivisor.
Negative tensor powers of I mean powers of its dual.
T is replete.
J is locally finitely generated; C is derived J-complete.
proofSteps: Use the replete-sheaf cohomology criterion supplied by E4 from the affine DD.1 theory.
The map H^i(C)→H^i(C) tensor I^(-1) has complete source and target. Its kernel is complete; the quotient by that kernel is complete.
Tensor with the invertible line I^⊗i, locally a free rank-one module, and apply the cohomology criterion again.
acceptance: Closure is under kernels/cokernels of maps BETWEEN complete modules and extensions; arbitrary submodules are not covered.
This statement does not commute Lη_I with J-completion.

nodes.title: Completion at the décalage ideal
nodes.statement: For derived I-completion C→Ĉ, the canonical comparison completion_I(Lη_I C)→Lη_I Ĉ is a quasi-isomorphism.
hypotheses: (T,O) is a ringed topos.
I is an invertible ideal subsheaf of O, locally generated by a nonzerodivisor.
Negative tensor powers of I mean powers of its dual.
T is replete.
proofSteps: The target is complete by preservation-derived-completeness, so the map extends along the completion unit.
On a principal chart both objects are derived f-complete; reduce the comparison modulo f by derived Nakayama.
Completion preserves the mod-f² coefficient sequence and its mod-f reduction, so the cohomology classes and Bockstein agree. Apply bockstein-reduction.
Glue the comparison using the sheaf completion interface.
acceptance: The ideal is I on BOTH sides; an unrelated J is excluded.
This inherited ID now names the first map of Lemma 6.20; its second map is completion-limit-model.

nodes.title: Inverse-limit comparison
nodes.statement: The canonical map Lη_I Ĉ→Rlim_n Lη_I(C tensor^L O/I^n) is a quasi-isomorphism, where Ĉ is derived I-completion.
hypotheses: (T,O) is a ringed topos.
I is an invertible ideal subsheaf of O, locally generated by a nonzerodivisor.
Negative tensor powers of I mean powers of its dual.
T is replete.
proofSteps: All objects are derived I-complete; derived tensor with O/I commutes with this limit because O/I has the finite flat resolution [I→O].
Locally use f and a complex D of O/f-modules. Compute D tensor^L O/f^n using [O --f^n→O], so it has the zero-differential extra shifted summand.
The transition n+1→n is identity on the unshifted summand and multiplication by f on the shifted summand, hence zero there on D. The extra pro-system is pro-zero.
This identifies the mod-f Bockstein towers; the inverse-limit and repleteness comparison is requested from E2/E4. Conclude by the complete-object reduction criterion.
acceptance: Do not replace the derived tensor factors by naive quotients of a torsion complex.
Record the transition maps: a termwise splitting alone does not prove a pro-isomorphism.

nodes.title: Injectivity before completion
nodes.statement: Let B=Q[x], M=direct sum over n≥0 of B e_n, and S(e_0)=0, S(e_(n+1))=e_n. The B-linear endomorphism F=S−x is injective on M.
proofSteps: For a nonzero finite sequence a choose the largest N in its support.
The coefficient of e_N in F(a) is −x a_N. It is nonzero because B is a domain and a_N≠0.
acceptance: The same assertion fails on the x-adic completion, as computed below.
This lemma does not use a finite-dimensional truncation with an artificial boundary condition.

nodes.title: Completion of the test module
nodes.statement: With B,M as above, let A=B[t] act on M by t=F. The derived (x)-completion of M[0] is concentrated in degree zero and equals N={(a_n) in product Q[[x]] : for each r, all but finitely many a_n lie in x^r Q[[x]]}. The A-action extends by t(a)_n=a_(n+1)−x a_n.
proofSteps: The endomorphism F is B-linear, so polynomial evaluation defines an A-module structure. Both x and t are nonzerodivisors of A; x is injective on M.
The free A-resolution [A --x^r→A] of A/x^r shows M tensor^L A/x^r=(M/x^rM)[0].
The quotient transition maps are surjective, so their derived limit is their ordinary limit in degree zero. Use the regular-principal completion comparison from DD.1.
Taking coordinates identifies this inverse limit with N: each finite-level vector has finite support; conversely this support condition makes every truncation a finite vector.
Shift and multiplication by x preserve the restricted-sequence condition and agree with the original action on finite sequences.
acceptance: N is a restricted product, not the entire product.
The natural map M→N is the usual coefficientwise inclusion.

nodes.title: Kernel created by completion
nodes.statement: For N and F in restricted-sequence-completion, ker F={ (a,xa,x²a,...) : a in Q[[x]] }. This kernel is nonzero.
proofSteps: The equation F(v)=0 is v_(n+1)=x v_n; induction gives v_n=x^n v_0.
Every such sequence satisfies the restricted condition: n≥r implies x^n a is divisible by x^r.
Choose a=1 to obtain a nonzero kernel element whose zeroth coordinate is 1.
acceptance: No convergence of a numerical series is being assumed: the condition is x-adic divisibility of coordinates.

nodes.title: Failure of unrelated completion
nodes.statement: For A=Q[x,t], I=(t), J=(x), and the module M defined above, the canonical map completion_J(Lη_t M[0])→Lη_t(completion_J M[0]) is not a quasi-isomorphism. On H^0 it is N→N/N[t], with nonzero kernel generated as Q[[x]]-module by (1,x,x²,...).
proofSteps: F is injective on M, so Lη_t M[0]=M[0]. Its derived J-completion is N[0].
The cohomology formula gives Lη_t N[0]=(N/N[t])[0].
Naturality of the quotient formula and the completion adjunction identify the canonical comparison with the quotient map N→N/N[t].
The displayed kernel is nonzero, so that comparison is not a quasi-isomorphism.
acceptance: This refutes the canonical comparison, not the stronger claim that the two objects can never be abstractly isomorphic.
Noetherianity of A does not repair the example: M is not finitely generated.
Finite truncations v_N=sum_(n<N)x^n e_n satisfy F(v_N)=−x^N e_(N−1), recording the disappearing defect.
